title: The Tijuana night in Beneath the Underdog
summary: Johnson asks if it happened as written; Mingus says yes and talks of Dannie Richmond.

blocks.x: But, anyway, the -- in rereading Beneath the Underdog, I came to that famous night in Tijuana

or wherever it was, with you and Danny Richmond. And I guess that was the most controversial part of that book. And just between you and me and the Smithsonian Institution, Charles, is that how it really went down?
Yeah, man. In fact, to tell you the truth, man, I think I beat my record with one woman one time, with my wife, with Sue.
(Inaudible.) [I'm glad he mentioned the right name there.]
That's not so great. Anybody can feel virile by having a different woman every time. But to make it with one person is the most -- should be the most admirable points.
Provided she's up to it, that is.
Yeah. Yes. Those were the days.
Well, they say if you -- as long as you keep active, you'll stay active.
Just like I wrote in the book, Danny Richmond, if he had had more money, he would have broke my record, not because he's a glutton. I was a glutton, I was just trying to get something off my chest.
In a manner of speaking. Anything else you --
Danny had -- contributed to 17 prostitutes. Yeah, 17, 18, 19, 20, 21 -- I'm sure he could have broke my record. If he had the money.
This is how records are made, right? It's true in more ways than one.
Yeah, I guess you have to read a book to know what we're talking about. They could always write a book.
